about: Route vectors for the workspace advertisement in config.json.
Authored in canopy (tests/canopy_mcp/fixtures/workspace/); every other holder keeps a byte-identical copy of the whole directory.
ASCII-only, no trailing whitespace, exactly one final newline.
Route vectors for the workspace's HTTP surface on FRONT. path is relative to the advertised workspace path (config.json workspace.path); there is no route that accepts commands.

Each case: setup steps (the scenarios' step grammar, on a fresh hub with epoch e1 and the clock at 0), one request {method, path, headers?, body?, padTo?}, expect {status, body?, events?}, then optional follow-up steps.

A body {'$file': <name>} is that fixture file's body (state.sample.json, state.oversize.json, state.reduced.json); state '$sample' / '$empty' as in the scenarios. padTo: once those are resolved, the body's compact JSON followed by spaces up to that many bytes.
A claim or report body is {windowId, seq, shown, state, truncated?}; truncated is true when the window reduced an oversize state. An error body is {code, detail}; expect names the code only.
Every workspace route, the event stream included, refuses a Sec-Fetch-Site that is present and neither same-origin nor none with 403 cross_site, before it reads the body or the hub.
Bodies are at most 131072 bytes (413 too_large); a state that breaks the hub's normalisation is 422 invalid_state.
optIn: the explicit CANOPY_* opt-in (off by default). Off: config.json has no workspace key and every workspace route is 404.

cases.name: the opt-in on advertises the path and protocol 1
the opt-in off: POST claim is 404
the opt-in off: PUT active is 404
the opt-in off: DELETE active?window=w-A is 404
the opt-in off: GET events?window=w-A is 404
the opt-in off: POST active/w-A/result is 404
